chunks: And Ibn Abī ʿUmayr narrated from Al-Ḥusayn ibn Khālid Al-Ṣayrafī, from Abū Al-Ḥasan Al-Māḍī, peace be upon him, who said:
I wrote to him regarding a man who died, and he had an umm walad, and her master had given her something during his lifetime, then he died.

He said: So he, peace be upon him, wrote: “She is entitled to what her master gave her during his lifetime; that is recognized as hers. The testimony concerning that of a man, a woman, and servants who are not accused is accepted.”

key_terms.أُمُّ وَلَدٍ: a bondwoman who has borne a child to her master
key_terms.سَيِّدُهَا: her master, the one who gave her the property
key_terms.شَهَادَةُ: legal testimony used to establish a claim
key_terms.شَيْئًا: some item or property granted to her
key_terms.غَيْرِ ٱلْمُتَّهَمِينَ: those not under suspicion of dishonesty or bias
key_terms.فِي حَيَاتِهِ: during his lifetime, before death and estate division
key_terms.ٱلْخَدَمِ: servants whose testimony may be considered

ai.seo_question: Is the testimony of women and servants accepted to prove property given to an umm walad before her master’s death?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling about property granted during a master's lifetime to an umm walad after his death. It affirms her right to what was given to her and establishes that testimony from a man, a woman, and non-suspect servants may be accepted in proving that claim.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.3314 - And Ibn Abi Umair narrated from Al-Husayn bin Khalid Al-Sayrafi, from Abu Al-Hasan Al-Madhi, peace be upon him, who said:
I wrote to Imam (as) regarding a man who died, leaving behind a bondwoman, and her master had given her something during his lifetime. Then the master died.

Imam (as) wrote back: "She is entitled to what her master gave her during his lifetime, as it is recognized for her. The testimony of a man, a woman, and trustworthy servants is accepted in this matter, provided they are not accused of dishonesty."
